STAGE 1

Write the whole-module specification

InputClean RTL module: rtlpp_10544_combined.v
InstructionDescribe the whole module’s interface and observable behavior in self-contained prose.

Protocol summary; exact prompt wording is retained by the evaluation runner, not this historical import.

OutputGenerated whole-module specification (prose).
Read input: rtlpp_10544_combined.v · Open raw
module rtlpp_10544(clk, 
               flash, 
               Hexs, 
               LES, 
               point, 
               rst, 
               Start, 
               SW0, 
               seg_clk, 
               seg_clrn, 
               SEG_PEN, 
               seg_sout);

    input clk;
    input flash;
    input [31:0] Hexs;
    input [7:0] LES;
    input [7:0] point;
    input rst;
    input Start;
    input SW0;
    output seg_clk;
    output seg_clrn;
    output SEG_PEN;
    output seg_sout;

    wire [63:0] XLXN_14;
    wire [63:0] XLXN_15;
    wire [63:0] XLXN_16;
    
    // Logic for P2S
    reg [63:0] shift_reg;
    reg [5:0] counter;
    wire shift_clk;

    assign seg_clk = clk;
    assign seg_clrn = ~rst;
    assign shift_clk = (Start & SEG_PEN) ? clk : 1'b0;
    
    always @(posedge shift_clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            shift_reg <= 64'b0;
            counter <= 6'b0;
        end else begin
            if (counter < 64) begin
                shift_reg <= {shift_reg[62:0], 1'b0};
                counter <= counter + 1;
            end else begin
                shift_reg <= XLXN_14;
                counter <= 6'b0;
            end
        end
    end
    
    assign seg_sout = shift_reg[63];
    
    // Logic for HexTo8SEG8
    integer i, j;
    reg [7:0] SEG_ARRAY [7:0]; // 8 bytes for 8 segments
    
    always @* begin
        for (i = 0; i < 8; i = i + 1) begin
            case (Hexs[i*4+3 -: 4])
                4'd0: SEG_ARRAY[i] = 8'b11000000;
                4'd1: SEG_ARRAY[i] = 8'b11111001;
                4'd2: SEG_ARRAY[i] = 8'b10100100;
                4'd3: SEG_ARRAY[i] = 8'b10110000;
                4'd4: SEG_ARRAY[i] = 8'b10011001;
                4'd5: SEG_ARRAY[i] = 8'b10010010;
                4'd6: SEG_ARRAY[i] = 8'b10000010;
                4'd7: SEG_ARRAY[i] = 8'b11111000;
                4'd8: SEG_ARRAY[i] = 8'b10000000;
                4'd9: SEG_ARRAY[i] = 8'b10010000;
                4'd10: SEG_ARRAY[i] = 8'b10001000;
                4'd11: SEG_ARRAY[i] = 8'b10000011;
                4'd12: SEG_ARRAY[i] = 8'b11000110;
                4'd13: SEG_ARRAY[i] = 8'b10100001;
                4'd14: SEG_ARRAY[i] = 8'b10000110;
                4'd15: SEG_ARRAY[i] = 8'b10001110;
                default: SEG_ARRAY[i] = 8'b11111111;
            endcase
        end
        
        // Applying flash, points, and LES
        for (j = 0; j < 8; j = j + 1) begin
            if (flash)
                SEG_ARRAY[j] = 8'b11111111;
            
            if (point[j])
                SEG_ARRAY[j] = SEG_ARRAY[j] & 8'b01111111; // Turn on point
            
            if (LES[j])
                SEG_ARRAY[j] = SEG_ARRAY[j] & 8'b11101111; // Turn on LES
        end
    end
    
    assign XLXN_16 = {SEG_ARRAY[7], SEG_ARRAY[6], SEG_ARRAY[5], SEG_ARRAY[4], SEG_ARRAY[3], SEG_ARRAY[2], SEG_ARRAY[1], SEG_ARRAY[0]};

    // Logic for MUX2T1_64
    assign XLXN_14 = SW0 ? XLXN_16 : XLXN_15;
   
    // Logic for SSeg_map
    reg [7:0] Seg_map [7:0]; // 8 segments
    
    always @* begin
        for (i = 0; i < 8; i = i + 1) begin
            Seg_map[i] = Hexs[i*4+3 -: 4] + 8'h30; // Add 0x30 to convert to ASCII
        end
    end
    
    assign XLXN_15 = {Seg_map[7], Seg_map[6], Seg_map[5], Seg_map[4], Seg_map[3], Seg_map[2], Seg_map[1], Seg_map[0]};
    
endmodule

Generate the module

InputThe generated Stage 1 specification plus the required top-module name rtlpp_10544.
InstructionImplement the complete synthesizable RTL module from the generated specification.

Protocol summary; the Stage 2 runner creates a fresh prompt.

OutputReconstructed complete RTL module.
Stage 1 output → abstraction gate → fresh Stage 2 input. The intermediate text is generated separately for each model/attempt. It is not a prefilled golden description. Stage 2 receives neither the clean RTL nor the Stage 1 conversation.
